paper_title: Spatial Audio Generation and Editing with Executable Plans and Self-Distilling Transfusion

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Spatial audio authoring coordinates source decisions with soundfield synthesis. For editing, plans specify what to change and retain, while reference audio supplies further acoustic detail. We present AMBIT, a unified framework for native First-Order Ambisonics (FOA) generation and editing with three connected contributions. First, a shared Transfusion backbone couples autoregressive planning with rectified-flow rendering through executable ScenePlans that specify source content, activity, and 3D trajectories. For editing, the plan describes the full target scene, including retained sources; contrastive features ground the requested change, while full reference latents supply residual acoustic detail for preservation. Second, an FOA-aware continuous VAE combines shared-decoder omnidirectional recovery, asymmetric grouped KL, and spatial covariance matching to preserve content and inter-channel structure. Third, joint Transfusion on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) refines planning on student-generated prefixes and rendering at sampling states reached under student plans, with target-conditioned teachers supervising both modes of the shared student. Evaluations across speech, music, and sound show improved generation content and spatial quality, acoustic fidelity during instruction-guided editing, and unedited-source preservation over the compared baselines. Project page: https://wjm-george.github.io/AMBIT/

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Spatial audio authoring supports immersive media, virtual acoustics, and interactive environments (Zhu et al., 2025) through text-driven generation and instruction-guided editing. Both tasks require decisions about what each source produces, when it is active, and how it moves to be realized in coherent soundfield (Guo et al., 2025a). Editing adds further requirement: changing selected attributes while retaining the surrounding sources. An executable plan can state both the requested change and the sources to keep at the semantic and structural level; reference audio then supplies residual acoustic detail beyond these symbolic fields. This motivates learning source decisions and multichannel synthesis together, with plans governing what changes or stays and reference latents supporting the acoustic preservation of retained sources. Recent work provides increasingly rich spatial audio controls. ImmerseDiffusion synthesizes First-Order Ambisonics (FOA) soundscapes from text and spatial, temporal, and environmental conditions using latent diffusion (Heydari et al., 2025). SonicMotion extends FOA generation to moving sound sources with explicit trajectory control (Templin et al., 2026). SwanWeave follows natural language instructions to edit content, timing, and spatial attributes of existing FOA scenes (Lei et al., 2026a). Unified authoring brings these capabilities together: language intent, source attributes, and rendered acoustics must remain aligned as scenes are generated and modified with source-level instructions. (i) Grounding language in 3D source controls. AudioChat explores stereo planning (Chen et al., 2026); FOA authoring requires source-bound content, timing, and 3D motion, with edit targets identified from source audio. (ii) Preserving acoustics and spatial structure in compact latents. Continuous FOA autoencoders support generation, while discrete codecs provide spatial-consistency supervision (Heydari et al., 2025; Sudarsanam et al., 2025). Yet, channel-wise reconstruction fails to explicitly supervise inter-channel energy, coherence, and phase. (iii) Refining discrete planning and continuous rendering. Paired training uses reference prefixes and target plans, whereas inference relies on student predictions. predicted plan changes both the conditions given to the renderer and the sampling states it encounters. DiffusionOPSD (Zhou et al., 2026) refines continuous generators without discrete token supervision. Joint refinement needs token and audio targets on student prefixes and visited sampling states. We introduce AMBIT (Figure 1), unified FOA authoring framework with three contributions. (i) Source-grounded Transfusion planning and rendering. Executable SCENEPLANs specify source content, timing, and motion. Their deterministically compiled controls connect autoregressive planning to rectified-flow rendering (Ma et al., 2025) within shared backbone. sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: Figure 1: Overview of AMBIT capabilities. (1) Spatial audio generation creates multi-source 3D scenes from text, controlling content, timing, and trajectories. (2) Instruction-guided spatial and temporal editing modifies selected sources, preserving unmodified content and spatial structure. retained sources are both explicit in the plan; semantic and spatial contrastive features ground the requested change, while full reference latents provide residual acoustic detail for the preservation of unchanged sources. (ii) An FOA-aware continuous Variational Autoencoder. The latents retain acoustics and inter-channel structure. Auxiliary reconstruction reuses the decoder, and asymmetric grouped KL gives latent group weaker regularization for recovery. Spatial covariance matching supervises relative energy, coherence, and phase between channels. (iii) Joint Transfusion On-Policy Self-Distillation. We adapt on-policy self-distillation (Zhao et al., 2026b; Jiang et al., 2026a) to both modes, with student plans driving DiT trajectories; frozen teachers use target plan memory and target audio reference tokens to supervise student prefixes and visited states. Token and clean-latent losses update shared and task-specific parameters, coupling updated plans to rendering conditions and states in fresh rollouts. For music and sound generation, AMBIT achieves higher paired CLAP and lower FAD than AudioX-Turbo (Tian et al., 2026a), while achieving the lowest speech WER and CER. Spatially, it reduces directional and binaural errors over TangoFlux (Hung et al., 2026) with spatialization. For editing, it outperforms SwanWeave (Lei et al., 2026a) in acoustic fidelity and spatial accuracy. Fixed-renderer comparisons support our planner, and VAE ablations improve reconstruction and spatial accuracy. Joint OPSD leads continued SFT, ReFL, and GRPO across all nine metrics.

sections.title: 2 RELATED WORK
sections.content: Spatial audio generation and representation. General-purpose and multimodal generators broaden audio content and conditioning (Liu et al., 2024; Evans et al., 2025; Tian et al., 2026b;a; 2025; Hung et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2026b), while timing-aware methods introduce event-level temporal control (Xie et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2025; 2026b). Diff-SAGe, DualSpec, and PhysWave (Kushwaha et al., 2025; Zhao et al., 2026a; Yao et al., 2026) explore category and location conditioning, joint spectrogram modeling, and directionand distance-consistency priors, respectively. Videoconditioned and trajectory-aware models further extend FOA synthesis (Kim et al., 2025; 2026; Lei et al., 2026b). Neural audio codecs (Kumar et al., 2023; Défossez et al., 2023; Ji et al., 2025) and continuous FOA autoencoders (Heydari et al., 2025) provide compact representations, while FOA Tokenizer incorporates spatial consistency supervision into discrete compression (Sudarsanam et al., 2025). AMBIT combines source-level 3D control with acoustic fidelity across native FOA generation and editing. Our VAE supervises acoustic reconstruction and inter-channel consistency. Audio editing and executable scene planning. AudioSpa and TAS offer text-guided mono-to-binaural spatialization (Feng et al., 2025; Pan et al., 2025c). Diffusion editing uses noise perturbation, inversion, or instruction conditioning (Meng et al., 2022; Manor and Michaeli, 2024; Jia et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2023; Pan et al., 2026). MMEdit, Audio-Omni, and SmartDJ (Tao et al., 2025; Tian et al., 2026c; Lan et al., 2025) extend language-guided editing, while SwanWeave targets native FOA editing (Lei et al., 2026a). Following Transfusion (Zhou et al., 2025), AMBIT unifies autoregressive planning and native FOA flow rendering. Executable, grammar-constrained SCENEPLANs bind content, activity, and 3D paths, compiling deterministically into source-indexed semantic and frame-aligned spatial controls. Audiotext contrastive learning aids grounding (Elizalde et al., 2023; Wu et al., 2023; Seki et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2025b). FOA features ground edits; reference latents support preservation. On-policy refinement and self-distillation. Preference optimization and reinforcement learning improve audio generation (Majumder et al., 2024; Li et al., 2026b); ReFL adds differentiable reward feedback (Xu et al., 2023). GRPOs group-relative advantages (Shao et al., 2024) extend to flow and diffusion generators (Liu et al., 2025b; Xue et al., 2025). On-policy distillation supervises student-generated sequences (Agarwal et al., 2024), with self-distillation for LLM reasoning (Zhao et al., 2026b) and continuous generators (Zhang et al., 2026a; Zhou et al., 2026; Jiang et al., 2026a; Liu et al., 2026). Transfusion OPSD instead jointly refines shared FOA editors discrete planner and continuous renderer. Frozen planning and rendering teachers use target plan memory and target audio to supply token distributions on student prefixes and clean-latent targets at flow states reached by rendering the students own plans.

An executable plan specifies the target scene; reference audio supplies acoustic context for editing. Mode-specific interfaces use causal attention for plan tokens and bidirectional attention for rendering latents. Executable SCENEPLAN interface. SCENEPLAN is the executable interface between source decisions and rendering. It specifies scene duration and room type, binding each sources type (speech, music, or sound), description, optional transcript, active interval, and static or linear 3D trajectory in azimuth, elevation, and distance. For editing, the planner predicts the complete target scene, including both modified and retained source attributes. SCENEPLAN compilation. The compiler deterministically forms source text clauses and aligns activity and pose to latent frames (Appendix B.1). Condition encoding uses frozen text backbone with learned projection and source role embeddings to produce cross-attention tokens cattn. Learned event embeddings encode interval-overlap activity; trajectory MLP encodes poses at frame midpoints. The spatial embeddings form R256T over latent frames. Together they yield C(S) = (cattn(S), c(S)) with semantic tokens and frame-aligned source controls. AMBIT CLAP for source understanding. Following CLAP (Elizalde et al., 2023; Wu et al., 2023), we learn separate semantic and scene alignment heads from frozen AMBIT VAE latents: Lalign = Lsem + λsceneLscene, (2) Both terms use symmetric audiotext contrastive losses with multiple positives. Semantic alignment matches content and source counts; scene alignment, weighted by λscene, also matches timing, spatial attributes, and room properties. Content-preserving spatial edits remain semantic positives but become scene negatives. The frozen encoder supplies global and temporal features (zs) for semantic and spatial grounding in the editing planner (Appendix B.3).

sections.title: 4.1 EXPERIMENTAL SETUP
sections.content: Datasets. Training uses 1.6M synthetic and recorded FOA examples and 1M editing pairs, covering speech, music, and environmental sounds. The AMBIT VAE is pretrained on 1M FOA clips. Evaluation uses 8,000 generation requests, 5,000 editing pairs, and 2,000 VAE test clips. Appendices and specify the data and evaluation protocols. Model and training. AMBIT uses 15 shared Transfusion blocks (width 1,024, 16 attention heads) for native FOA generation and editing. The shared backbone, native AR/DiT interfaces, and structured heads total 332.6M trainable parameters. Joint supervised training uses token and rectified flow objectives with AdamW at 104 for adapters and heads and 2 106 for shared blocks. Paired rendering uses ground-truth plans; inference uses AR predictions. The Qwen3.5-0.8B text backbone (Qwen Team, 2026), AMBIT CLAP, and AMBIT VAE remain frozen. OPSD uses AdamW with global batch of 64 requests and loss weights λAR = 0.1, λDiT = 1, and λref = 0.1, with prepared teachers frozen. sections.title: 4.5 POST-TRAINING WITH OPSD
sections.content: Post-training should improve how scene decisions are realized in audio. We compare OPSD configurations with continued SFT, our ReFL adaptation (Xu et al., 2023), and two branch GRPO (Shao et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025b) under identical evaluation settings (Appendix E.5). Joint OPSD leads all reported metrics  (Table 6)  . DiT OPSD improves every metric over SFT, whereas AR OPSD improves only LSD and FSAD. The gains across content, reconstruction, and binaural metrics support refining planning and rendering together within the shared editing model. further question is whether on-policy planning distillation adds to rendering refinement under student plans. We contrast joint OPSD with the two supervision variants. AR OPSD retains GT plans for flow supervision; DiT OPSD retains GT token supervision while distilling rendering under student plans. These plans determine both DiT conditions and the states queried for distillation. Joint OPSD adds planning distillation on student prefixes; all variants update the shared Transformer. Further reductions in classifier KL and CRW over DiT OPSD support combining planning and rendering distillation on student prefixes and visited states, improving content fidelity and spatial execution. sections.title: 5 CONCLUSION AND LIMITATIONS
sections.content: We presented AMBIT, unified Transfusion framework for native FOA generation and editing. Executable SCENEPLANs connect source-level content, timing, and motion to continuous rendering, stating both requested edits and retained sources; contrastive features ground the change, while full reference latents supply residual acoustic detail for preservation. Our FOA-aware VAE combines omnidirectional recovery with inter-channel supervision, and joint Transfusion OPSD refines planning and rendering on student-generated contexts. Experiments across speech, music, and sound show improvements in content fidelity, spatial accuracy, and unedited-source preservation. Joint OPSD further improves all nine reported metrics over continued supervised training, ReFL, GRPO, and both branch supervision variants. These results support jointly learning scene control and acoustic execution for spatial audio authoring. Our current SCENEPLAN configuration supports scenes up to approximately 15 s. Extending AMBIT to longer soundscapes and evaluating acoustic consistency across successive edits remain important directions for future work.

sections.content: D.1 EVALUATION PROTOCOL AND BASELINE INTERFACES Generation and editing results use the 8k generation and 5k editing benchmarks, respectively. The AMBIT VAE is evaluated on 2,000 FOA clips. Music, Sound, and Speech categories can overlap; pooled spatial results count each scene once. Audio comparisons use executable plans and metric valid observations from the relevant benchmark; missing measurements are excluded rather than assigned zero error. External generators receive semantic descriptions, while AMBIT receives qualitative requests. Editing baselines use source audio and an instruction or target description according to their native interfaces. Qwen3-Omni is planner for our DiT, distinct from the Audio-Omni editor: its source observation is the waveform, whereas AMBIT uses native FOA features. D.2 EXTERNAL AUDIO SPATIALIZATION For BEWO + AS and TangoFlux + AS in Table 4, Qwen3.5-4B supplies the same executable plans to both systems. Each audio backend synthesizes source signals from the plans semantic fields; these signals are downmixed to mono and placed within their predicted activity intervals. Pyroomacoustics renders the predicted positions and room classes in ACN/SN3D FOA, using fixed inference geometry instead of ground truth room dimensions. Moving sources crossfade room responses at 250ms intervals. Qwen3.5-4B + DiT instead passes its plan through our compiler and neural renderer. These comparisons assess complete planning and rendering systems with common target waveform. D.3 METRICS The generation, editing, and VAE test sets contain 8,000 requests, 5,000 requests, and 2,000 clips, respectively. All systems use the same evaluation examples for each task and metric. Directional errors use common set of frames with valid direction estimates in the reference and every compared output. Object metrics additionally use isolated source intervals. Content and speech. Paired CLAP measures similarity between output and reference audio. FAD and feature based Fréchet distances compare embedding distributions; PANNs/PaSST KL compares predicted acoustic classes. Distributional scores use the evaluated features directly. Generation uses native or arithmetic mean mono, peak normalized to 1 dBFS before resampling; editing uses mono downmixes of binauralized FOA without gain normalization. CLAP, PANNs, and VGGish operate at 48, 32, and 16 kHz. For clips longer than 10 s, CLAP window embeddings are normalized, averaged, and renormalized. Distil-Whisper large-v3 supplies transcriptions; generation WER/CER aggregate edit counts over reference lengths (Zhang et al., 2025e), while UTMOS averages individual clip scores.

They rated editing on overall audio quality, edit success, and preservation of unedited content. Each dimension used five-point scale from 1 (very poor) to 5 (excellent). Table 12 reports the mean of valid ratings for each system and dimension. The same participant rated all three outputs for each case under the same request and playback setup, enabling within-case comparison. Results. AMBIT outperforms both baselines in mean listener ratings across all seven measures. For generation, it achieves scores of 3.11 in overall quality, 3.25 in instruction adherence, 3.37 in spatial adherence, and 3.03 in spatial naturalness. Its largest advantage is in spatial adherence, where it exceeds the strongest baseline by 0.54 points, followed by 0.29-point gain in instruction adherence. For editing, AMBIT achieves 3.64 in overall quality, 3.57 in edit success, and 3.71 in preservation of unedited content, exceeding Qwen3-Omni + DiT by 0.13, 0.31, and 0.27 points, respectively. These results highlight AMBITs strengths in following spatial instructions and carrying out requested edits while preserving the surrounding audio content.
